name: empty_like
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::empty_like(Tensor self, *, ScalarType? dtype=None, Layout? layout=None, Device? device=None, bool? pin_memory=None, MemoryFormat? memory_format=None) -> Tensor. Original Gems pytest owns the full contract: it exercises this default overload together with the registered out overload, their keyword arguments (dtype, layout, device, pin_memory, memory_format, out), returns (a single Tensor; the .out overload returns the out buffer itself), error/rejection behavior (string memory_format/dtype, channels_last on 2-D, channels_last_3d on 2-D, sparse layout, pin_memory=True on a device tensor, non-tensor input) and aliasing/mutation behavior; do not narrow those tests to this one signature. All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: aten::empty_like(Tensor self, *, ScalarType? dtype=None, Layout? layout=None, Device? device=None, bool? pin_memory=None, MemoryFormat? memory_format=None) -> Tensor ; aten::empty_like.out(Tensor self, *, MemoryFormat? memory_format=None, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Semantics derived from the tests: allocate fresh, uninitialized storage shaped like the input tensor, reproducing its size, dtype by default, strides and memory layout (preserve_format default, or the requested memory_format; zero strides are not carried over and the result starts at storage offset 0). The positive override cases are the dtype rows (int32, float64); the device-override row requests the input's own device, and pin_memory is exercised positively only with pin_memory=False, while pin_memory=True on a device tensor appears only as a rejection. An allocation builds no autograd graph, the output's conj/neg flags are compared against the reference rather than asserted to be absent, and the output does not alias the input. Under deterministic algorithms with fill_uninitialized_memory the fresh allocation is filled so its contents become defined. The .out overload writes into the caller's buffer and returns it, resizing a smaller buffer in place, and is therefore overload-dependent (effects below describe the representative default overload only, which mutates nothing and returns no alias). Non-JSON ATen defaults: not applicable here, since every optional default in the representative schema is JSON null and was preserved as null.
